content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% immediately after spike, then apply mean reversion over next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in the last 5–7 days of the forecast horizon; if true outcome shows upward trend, model should not overreact; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- Forecast lags true price movements by 2–4 days; shift forecast forward by 1–2 days for the first 10–15 days of the horizon.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent low” — when history includes recent dips, forecasts stay too low; increase forecast by 1–3% if recent 7-day average is below 65.00.
